Non-durable goods are typically low-priced, purchased frequently, consumed quickly (often in one use), and involve minimal purchase risk because of their low cost and routine nature.  
Durable goods are long-lasting and higher-priced, so they don’t match.  
Generic goods refer to unbranded products, but they aren’t necessarily defined by being low-priced and frequently purchased in the same way.  
Luxury goods are high-priced and high-risk purchases, so they don’t fit either.  

Final answer: (A)
